404_record_not_found.description: GET /api/v1/statuses/:id (or any single-resource read) for a status that has been deleted, never existed, or belongs to an account that has blocked the caller — Mastodon answers the same way in all three cases so a blocked caller cannot tell which one happened.

403_not_permitted.description: POST /api/v1/statuses/:id/favourite for a status whose author the caller has blocked. StatusPolicy#favourite? is show? && !blocking_author?, and show? is still true (the caller blocked them, not the other way round), so this fails the policy check rather than the earlier not_found lookup and is never caught locally, so it reaches the app-wide handler.

403_insufficient_scope.description: Any write call (e.g. POST /api/v1/statuses/:id/favourite) made with a token that only has the 'read' scope. Doorkeeper raises before the request reaches application code.

body.error: This action is outside the authorized scopes

422_validation_failed.description: POST /api/v1/statuses with text longer than the server's character limit. ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid's message is 'Validation failed: ' followed by the humanized attribute name and the I18n text from statuses.over_character_limit.

body.error: Validation failed: Text character limit of 500 exceeded

429_rate_limited.description: Any API call once rack-attack's throttle for that family of endpoints has been used up. X-RateLimit-Reset is an ISO 8601 timestamp (with microseconds) for when the current throttle window ends, not a Unix epoch integer.
